title: Procurement law eased for 'deprived' bidders; TIB warns of abuse
excerpt: Parliament has made experience and turnover rules optional and created a 'deprived persons' category. TIB says it could be used for partisan ends.
content:
Parliament passed the Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Bill, 2026 by voice vote on 16 November, The Business Standard reported. Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury moved the bill, which was first placed before Parliament on 11 November.

New subsections 25(2) and 25(3) make long experience, high annual turnover and past large contracts optional requirements for bidders. A new Section 36A defines "deprived persons" as people who held valid licences or registrations in the past 20 years but could not take part in public procurement. The government can also relax tender rules for domestic industries, new bidders, micro and small enterprises, and women entrepreneurs.

Government procurement is worth roughly $30 billion a year. It makes up 45 percent of the national budget and 85 percent of Annual Development Programme spending, according to the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority's 2024-25 annual report, the paper said.

What experts said

  • Iftekharuzzaman, executive director of Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB): "The unprecedented introduction of the 'deprived' category could become a convenient tool for partisan abuse of power."
  • Zahid Hussain, former lead economist at the World Bank's Dhaka office: "Those previously excluded over irregularities can now participate and compete normally."
  • Faruk Hossain, former director general of the Central Procurement Technical Unit: "Awarding contracts to specific individuals cannot be the objective of a law."

Why it matters

Public contracts pay for the schools, clinics, roads and shelters that NGOs work alongside, so who wins them affects quality on the ground. Looser rules could open the door to small firms and women-led businesses, but TIB's warning points to a risk of contracts going to the politically connected.

What to watch

How the government defines and applies the "deprived" category in practice, and whether the procurement authority publishes data on who wins contracts under the new rules.

Sources

  • The Business Standard: Govt eases tender rules for 'deprived' bidders under amended procurement law, 17 November 2026
